subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron quarantine sidecars intentionally become regular-file-only persisted state, with oversized or incompatible existing targets requiring manual repair or removal before persistence resumes?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish that the hardening works, but tests cannot decide whether this stricter upgrade and recovery contract is acceptable for existing operator-visible persisted state.

options.title: Accept strict recovery contract
options.body: Approve the regular-file-only 8 MiB boundary and rely on a clearly communicated manual repair or removal path for incompatible sidecars.

options.title: Preserve prior target semantics
options.body: Use a byte-bounded reader that continues following previously accepted target types while retaining the matching save cap.

options.title: Add automated recovery
options.body: Keep the strict reader but add a bounded doctor migration or reset path for incompatible quarantine sidecars.

recommendation.title: Accept strict recovery contract
recommendation.body: Approve the regular-file-only 8 MiB boundary and rely on a clearly communicated manual repair or removal path for incompatible sidecars.

likelyOwner.reason: Original cron feature authorship and the strongest contribution history across the affected persistence and doctor paths make this the best available decision owner.
